ok got it, thanks. unrelated but: first 10k in 7 weeks, currently can run 5k in about 31 min. heres my plan for this week, too much?

mon rest
tue 5k easy
wed 6k tempo at 5:45/km
thu rest
fri 5k easy
sat 9k long
sun 3k recovery

thats 28k, last week i did 15k

I need to write a 1,500 word essay for a part time course I'm taking on the impact of remote work on company culture. I have lots of notes but I'm not sure how to organize them. Should I structure it by pros and cons, by theme, or chronologically with how things changed since 2020?

Thanks, that helps. Different topic: we're a small startup and I'm the PM for our internal Python tooling library. Engineers want to start publishing it to a private package index instead of copying files between repos. Could you help me put together a rough two-week plan for getting that working? It needs to cover the pyproject setup, virtualenvs for devs, pinning dependencies, and a release process. We have three engineers and one of them is new to packaging, so the plan should be simple enough for them to follow.

My parents are visiting from Hyderabad for three weeks starting November 8, staying with us in Austin. My mom will want to cook, but I'd also like to cook for them on weekends so they don't feel like they have to do everything. I'm fairly comfortable with dal and a couple of curries. Could you help me plan the cooking across the three weeks? Both my parents are vegetarian and my dad is diabetic.

Got it, thank you. Switching gears completely: I've been trying to perfect dal makhani at home and I'd love some feedback on my current recipe. It's tasty but not as creamy and rich as restaurant versions.

- 1 cup whole urad dal + 1/4 cup rajma, soaked overnight
- Pressure cooked with salt for 6 whistles
- Tadka: 2 tbsp butter, 1 onion, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 2 tomatoes pureed, 1 tsp Kashmiri chili, 1 tsp garam masala
- Add dal, simmer 15 minutes
- Finish with 2 tbsp cream

What would you change?

I've had trouble falling asleep for a few months now, usually lying awake for an hour or more. I work as a backend engineer with on-call shifts every fourth week. I put together a plan to fix it and would like your feedback:

1. Bedtime 11:00 pm, wake 7:00 am every day including weekends
2. No screens after 10:00 pm
3. Melatonin 10 mg at 10:30 pm
4. If I can't sleep after 20 minutes, get up and read in the living room
5. No coffee after 2 pm
6. Workout in the evening around 9 pm to tire myself out

Does this look reasonable?

Great, I'll go with that. Separately, my English teacher says the thesis has to go at the end of the intro paragraph, but when I read published essays it's often somewhere else. Why is the thesis placed where it is? I write a lot of technical docs at work so I want to understand the reasoning, not just memorize the rule.

Oh, another thing. I'm trying to clean up a feature branch before opening a PR. It has 14 commits, many of them like 'wip', 'fix typo' and 'address review'. Here's what I'm planning to do, could you check if it's right?

```
git fetch origin
git rebase -i origin/main
# mark all but the first commit as 'squash'
git push origin feature/payments-retry
```

The branch is only used by me, but I've already pushed it once.
my orders table has 20m rows and this query takes 40 sec: select * from orders where customer_id = 123 order by created_at desc limit 10. postgres. should i add an index or partition the table

random q but need ideas for finding a 2 bed rental under 2200 near a good elementary school, 2 kids. moving in 6 weeks. where do i even look

my F-1 visa got refused under 214(b) yesterday at the Mumbai consulate. interview was literally 2 minutes, the officer asked why this university and what I'd do after, and then just handed me the refusal slip. I have an admit for MS in Computer Science at Arizona State for Spring 2027 (starts January). Now I'm trying to decide between reapplying right away, deferring to Fall 2027, or switching to a different school I also got into (University of Texas at Dallas, also Spring). what should I do?

ok thanks. different thing, my DFS for a graph assignment crashes with RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded while calling a Python object. Works fine on the small test graph, dies on the big one (about 50,000 nodes, basically a long chain). I tried sys.setrecursionlimit(10000) and it still crashed, then I set it to 100000 and Python just died with no error at all. Should I keep raising the limit, rewrite it with a stack, or is there some other fix?

cool, will add it. ok so totally separate, I'm a senior graduating in May 2027, I have a return offer at $78k in Columbus, Ohio. I really want to buy a small house or condo within like 2 years instead of throwing money at rent. I tried one of those online pre-qualification things and it basically said I don't qualify for anything, which seems ridiculous given the salary. I have about $4,000 saved, one student credit card I've had for a year, and $22k in federal student loans. Can you help me make a plan?

I'm a freelance designer and this is my first year trying to handle advance tax properly. I opted for presumptive taxation under 44ADA. Here's my estimate for FY 2026-27 — could you check whether this looks right?

- Expected receipts: ₹18,00,000
- Taxable under 44ADA (50%): ₹9,00,000
- FD interest: ₹40,000
- Total: ₹9,40,000
- New regime tax: 0-4L nil, 4-8L 5% = 20,000, 8-9.4L 10% = 14,000, total 34,000 + 4% cess = ₹35,360
- Advance tax installments: 15% by June 15, 45% by Sept 15, 75% by Dec 15, 100% by March 15

Perfect, thanks. On another note, I'm a freelance designer who's learning React so I can build my own portfolio site. I've been going back and forth on whether to use plain React with Vite, or Next.js. Which would you recommend for a portfolio with about 6 pages and a blog?

Unrelated question: I've been having trouble sleeping lately, as I tend to wake up around 3am and can't fall back asleep. Could you explain what causes that? I'm a freelancer, so my schedule is irregular, and I drink about two coffees a day.
Quick one. I'm going to Lisbon for 5 days in October for a client workshop. Is it worth packing a light rain jacket or should I just bring an umbrella? I'm flying carry-on only.

I'm a backend engineer and I've been baking sourdough for about two months, so I like understanding the mechanisms. My loaves come out dense with a tight crumb even though the starter doubles in about 5 hours at 24C. I'm doing 75% hydration, 20% starter, 2% salt, bulk for 4 hours at 22C and a 12 hour fridge proof. Can you explain what causes the dense crumb, in terms of what's happening in the dough?

I'm a backend engineer taking a part-time MBA course and I have to write my first academic-style essay in years, argument about whether tech companies should be regulated like utilities, about 1,200 words. I tend to write like I code: lots of bullet points and no flow. How do I go about structuring and writing it step by step?

Got it. Totally unrelated: started SIPs in March in two funds via Kuvera, ₹10k each on the 5th, with an HDFC Bank autopay mandate. April and May went through fine. June and July both show 'Failed' in Kuvera, and the money's still sitting in my account, balance was well over 20k both times. Kuvera's status for the mandate just says 'Active'. HDFC netbanking shows the mandate too. What's going on and am I losing anything?

I'm a PM at a Series B fintech, about 4 years of PM experience, and I've got interview loops coming up for senior PM roles at two bigger companies in about 6 weeks. My product sense and execution answers felt loose in the last couple of screens. I'm trying to decide how to prep: paying for Exponent, working through Lewis Lin's 'Decode and Conquer', or doing peer mocks through a PM Slack community I'm in. Which would you pick?

Great, locking that in. Different question: I'm a PM at a Series B startup and I've been interviewing for a senior PM role at a larger company. They made an offer: $172k base, $40k/year RSUs, no signing bonus. I countered at $190k base plus a $20k signing bonus, citing a competing process. That was 6 days ago and the recruiter has gone completely silent. Two follow-up emails, no reply. Did I blow it?
